activity_context.topic_title: Projecting Vectors Onto Subspaces in Euclidean Spaces (Arbitrary Bases)

feedback.problem:
Find the vector in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ 
that is closest to the vector $x,$ where 

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly independent. 

The closest vector to $x$ in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace, which is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\,⇒\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}27 & -3 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{24}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 9\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6} \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
